claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. 

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions. Let me start by reading the official guidance to ensure I give you accurate information.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for waiting. Now I can help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To start, could you please tell me: **Do you have any children for whom you'd like to claim Child Benefit?** If yes, how many children?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child I'd like to claim for. His name is Alex, and he's 17.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I can see that Alex is 17 years old.

To assess eligibility for Alex, I need to know: **Is Alex currently in approved education or training?**

(For example, this could include school, college, A-levels, certain vocational courses, or approved training programs.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any approved education right now. He finished school but hasn't gone on to college or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. 

Since Alex is 17 and not in approved education or training, I need to understand his current situation better.

**Has Alex left education or training within the last 20 weeks, and if so, has he registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with the careers service or anything like that. He just left school and hasn't signed up with anyone.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information.

Just to clarify the timeline: **When did Alex leave school or approved education/training?** (For example, was it within the last 20 weeks, or longer ago than that?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It was more than 20 weeks ago - he left school a while back now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I now have a few more questions to complete the assessment.

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Now I need to ask: **Do you live with Alex, or are you paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after him?** 

(This could include contributions for things like food, clothes, or pocket money.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment.

**Has Alex started paid work for 24 hours or more per week?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working 24 hours a week or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question:

**Is Alex claiming any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't get any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for answering all my questions. Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why: While you normally qualify for Child Benefit for children under 16, for children aged 16-19, they must be staying in approved education or training. Since Alex is 17 and is not currently in approved education or training, he doesn't meet this requirement.

There is a provision that allows Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks after a 16 or 17 year old leaves education if they register with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services. However, since Alex left school more than 20 weeks ago and hasn't registered with either of these services, this extension period doesn't apply.

If Alex's circumstances change - for example, if he starts college, an apprenticeship, or other approved education or training - you may become eligible for Child Benefit at that point. You would need to check what counts as approved education or training and make a new claim if his situation changes.

I'm sorry this isn't the outcome you were hoping for. Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?

For children aged 16 or over, you'll normally still qualify if your child is under 20 AND they stay in approved education or training. Additionally, you can apply for Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services. In this case, Alex is 17 years old, which means he falls into the 16-20 age category. However, Alex is not currently in approved education or training. He left school more than 20 weeks ago and has not registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services. Since Alex does not meet the criteria for continued Child Benefit (not in approved education/training, and the 20-week extension period after leaving education has passed without registration with careers service/armed services), you are ineligible for Child Benefit for Alex. While you live with Alex in the UK and he is not working 24+ hours per week or claiming benefits in his own right, the fundamental requirement that he must be either under 16 OR (if 16-19) in approved education or training is not met.
